ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ortho-substituted benzene ring; the ortho position above the benzene ring is connected to a carboxylate group, drawn as CO2−; the adjacent position of the benzene ring is connected to a central carbon. This central carbon is also connected to a negatively charged oxygen O−, a hydroxyl group OH, and a nitrogen N containing H, and the nitrogen is further connected to R. The curved arrow in the figure indicates electron transfer, and the problem requires ignoring the arrow. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrow, the non-arrow molecular graph is a central carbon connected to N, [O-], O(H), and an ortho-carboxylate-substituted phenyl group. According to the specified encoding, the external R substituent of N is represented with the wildcard * as *N, the central carbon is written as C([O-])(O), connected to the aromatic ring c1ccccc1, and the aromatic ring ortho-carboxylate branch is written as C(=O)[O-]. Therefore the SMILES is *NC([O-])(O)c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-].

method.method_draft: First transcribe the non-arrow molecular graph from the image: central carbon bonded to N, [O-], O(H), and an ortho-carboxylated phenyl group. Encode the N-substituent as *N attached to that central carbon, write the central carbon as C([O-])(O), attach it to the aromatic ring, and place the ortho carboxylate branch on the ring as C(=O)[O-]. A canonical-style serialization is *NC([O-])(O)c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-].

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct structure-to-SMILES route: identify every atom and bond in the drawing, explicitly ignore the curved arrows, then serialize the resulting connectivity. It is the main honest solution path for this image-grounded conversion task.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the image as an ortho-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is a carboxylate group attached to the ring, drawn as CO2−, to be encoded as C(=O)[O-]. The adjacent ring carbon bears a tetrahedral carbon attached to three heteroatom substituents: N(H)R, O−, and OH. The curved arrows are reaction/transition-state annotations and are not part of the molecular graph. Treat R as an unspecified substituent represented by wildcard * bonded to N.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction to output the SMILES expression and specifically to ignore the arrows, so only the static connectivity and formal charges seen in the image are encoded.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard SMILES conventions: aromatic benzene is written with lowercase c atoms; an ortho-disubstituted benzene can be represented as c1ccccc1 with branches at adjacent positions; charged oxygens require bracket notation [O-]; neutral hydroxyl can be O; an unspecified R group is represented by *; branch parentheses encode substituents from the central tetrahedral carbon.
